address: Pórtico de Bajo de Guía 10, Sanlúcar de Barrameda, 11540, Spain
bio: This family-run restaurant opened its doors in 1951 as a simple seaside “taberna” serving Manzanilla sherry to the weather-beaten fishermen from the town’s Bajo de Guía district. Over the years, Fernando Bigote and his children have gradually expanded the business. Nowadays, it still boasts a typical “taberna”, where you can eat an array of tapas and “raciones”, as well as two neo-rustic dining rooms decorated in a maritime style, with the room upstairs perhaps the more impressive thanks to its views of the mouth of the Guadalquivir. Choose from delicious fried delicacies, fish and seafood stews, local fish and, above all, the spectacular Sanlúcar prawns for which the restaurant is renowned and which are a must here....
